articles.title: India's First High-Altitude Snow Leopard Safari Launched in Ladakh: Key Facts and Significance
articles.content: India’s First Snow Leopard Safari: India's first high-altitude Snow Leopard Wildlife Safari has been launched in Ladakh to promote responsible wildlife tourism and preserve the fragile habitat of this rare animal as well as to provide jobs to the local people. Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena inaugurated the programme during the Wildlife Week 2026. Initially, six specially designed vehicles will be used in snow leopard hotspots like Rumbak, Shang and Uley. Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation (SHAN) Society is organizing the safari in cooperation with Department of Forest, Ecology and Environment, Union Territory of Ladakh. The program will help to develop more organized and sustainable wildlife tourism, while also promoting the sustainable utilization of the region's natural resources for the benefit of local communities. Key Facts About India’s First Snow Leopard Safari Facts Details Name Ladakh Snow Leopard Safari Location Union Territory of Ladakh Significance India’s first high-altitude wildlife safari Launched by Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena Vehicles flagged off Six Initial locations Rumbak, Shang and Uley Implementing organisation Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation (SHAN) Society Government partner Department of Forest, Ecology and Environment, Ladakh Main objective Responsible tourism, wildlife conservation and local livelihoods Snow leopards estimated in India 718 Snow leopards estimated in Ladakh 477 Source: Administration of the Union Territory of Ladakh and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. Glad to announce India’s first-ever High-Altitude Wildlife Safari in Ladakh! In the first Governing Body meeting of the newly formed Snow Leopard & High-Altitude Nature (SHAN) Conservation Society, approved introducing guided Jeep safaris on popular snow-leopard and birdwatching trails across Hemis National Park, Changthang and Karakoram wildlife sanctuaries and landscapes like Drass, Nubra and Sham. The guided safari primarily aims at curbing incidents of illegal off-roading, disturbing the wildlife while boosting sustainable & responsible eco-tourism and enhancing visitor experience. This initiative is rooted in community-led conservation. By training local youth as specialized guides, empowering women artisans, and launching plastic-free campaigns, we are ensuring that local communities become equal partners in environment conservation and benefit economically. We are committed to preserve our greatest natural assets together, sustainably! — LG Ladakh (@lg_ladakh) August 6, 2026 What Is India’s First High-Altitude Snow Leopard Safari? The Ladakh Snow Leopard Safari is a guided safari that aims to let tourists explore the highlands and to watch the wildlife in a responsible manner. This safari will be conducted with specially made vehicles with open backs, local drivers and wildlife guides. Use of approved routes and restriction of visitor numbers is designed to minimise disturbance to animals and animal habitats. The project also aims to stop off-road activities like illegal off-road driving, which can harm the delicate mountain ecosystems and disrupt wildlife. The administration is not going to allow tourism activities to add further stress on nature, but will rather associate tourism with conservation and economic development.
